items.title: Conversational Artificial Intelligence in Community Care: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: The strategic shift toward community-based healthcare, away from hospital settings, is a policy priority internationally. Conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) may support this transition, yet its practical applications remain underexplored. This scoping review maps CAI capabilities and their configuration within community care. We searched PubMed, the ACM Digital Library, and selected grey-literature sources for studies published from January 2023 to June 2025. Of 551 records identified, 29 studies were included. We identified 20 capabilities across five functional domains: Understand (n = 5), Transform (n = 3), Remember (n = 3), Generate (n = 5), and Act (n = 4). Findings suggest that CAI extends rather than replaces human care, supporting access, ongoing engagement, and care coordination. Multi-party and expert-in-the-loop designs emerged as recurring implementation strategies. They also surface design tensions, including tradeoffs between reliability and conversational flexibility, and between the benefits of long-term memory and associated privacy risks. The resulting capability-centered taxonomy offers accessible framework for integrating CAI into community care settings.

items.title: Determining Voice Control Boundaries for in-Vehicle Functions: A User-Engineer-Expert Assessment Framework
items.abstract: Efficiently adapting voice control functions in smart vehicles remains a practical challenge in human-computer interaction. This study established a three-source, lightweight research system comprising user questionnaire survey (N = 326), engineer evaluation from the corporate sector (N = 12), and expert interviews from the industry (N = 8). A six-dimensional weighted adaptability assessment model(SWAAM) was designed (safety risk 30%, operational complexity 20%, usage frequency 15%, command clarity 15%, feedback requirements 10%, and technical feasibility 10%). Within 15 days, a systematic evaluation of 30 vehicle control functions was completed. The results indicate that user voice preference exhibits significant stratification: preference rates for high-frequency comfort functions such as navigation, air conditioning, and media exceed 98%, while preference rates for safety-critical functions such as driver assistance and chassis control are below 60%. Through triangulation validation, 15 items were identified for the whitelist (priority for release), 3 for the blacklist (prohibited from release), and 12 for the graylist (requiring scenario-based release, e.g., window control limited to speeds below 80 km/h, special scenario modes restricted to parking only). Expert consensus established safety red lines and design specifications, including “prohibition of voice control for core driving functions,” “adoption of the “action + object” command format,” and “requirement for secondary confirmation for safety-related functions.” The weighted total score across the six dimensions showed high consistency with the functional list (whitelist ≥ 7 points, blacklist <4.0 points), validating the model’s effectiveness. This method ensures scientific rigor while reducing the adaptation cycle to 15 days. It provides a practical, lightweight framework for rapid iteration in mass-production voice interaction projects.

items.title: Efficient Sensor Configuration for Accelerometer-Based Silent Speech Interfaces: Regionally Distributed Sensor Placement Strategy Considering Articulatory Dynamics
items.abstract: Silent speech interfaces (SSIs) decode articulatory activity without audible speech. Although accelerometer-based SSIs can capture facial and neck movements in compact wearable setups, accelerometer-specific sensor placement has not been systematically examined. This study evaluated all combinations of ten accelerometers across the lower face and neck in a 100 English word silent speech classification task with 20 participants. Subject-dependent classification was performed using a convolutional neural network followed by a bidirectional long short-term memory network. Accuracy improved as the number of sensors increased, reaching a plateau with five sensors. At this point, Sensors 1 and 7, positioned over the upper and lower labial regions, Sensors 4 and 8, located bilaterally along the buccal-mandibular region, and Sensor 5, placed over the left submental region beneath the chin, achieved the highest accuracy of 92.30 ± 4.64% and were selected as the efficient configuration. These five sensors consistently ranked among the most informative locations in standalone performance, perturbation-based explainability, and sensor ablation analyses, indicating that they contributed unique and influential articulatory information. Regional coverage comparisons showed that configurations spanning broader functional articulatory regions outperformed those with more restricted coverage. This placement strategy was further validated using an independent 100-word vocabulary, demonstrating that broad regional coverage remained advantageous despite slight changes in the optimal sensor identities. A practical three-sensor configuration based on this strategy achieved approximately 90% recognition accuracy while substantially reducing hardware complexity. Together, these results support regionally distributed sensor placement as a design strategy for capturing complementary articulatory information in compact accelerometer-based SSI systems.

items.title: From Vibe to Code—and Back: Lexical Oscillation in the Formation of Design Intent with Generative AI
items.abstract: Generative AI design tools make natural-language prompts a starting point for design, placing new articulation demands on designers. Rather than treating prompts as the transmission of preexisting intent, we ask how design intent is formed through situated interaction with AI. Five expert UI/UX designers (11–20 years’ experience, M = 15.4) designed landing-page hero sections with a generative AI tool, recorded through think-aloud and retrospective interviews. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we treated lexical granularity (L1 vibe, L2 design-domain, L3 operational language) as a sensitizing lens. Rather than moving from vibe to code unidirectionally, designers showed lexical oscillation, including returns from operational specificity to ambiguity. Mismatches with AI outputs became occasions to reconsider what they meant, and engagement shifted from instruction to consultation. One non-oscillating trajectory—a negative case—suggested conceptual misalignment as a tentative boundary. We position AI as a non-neutral generative interlocutor and ambiguity as a resource for design judgment.

items.title: Integrated Cognitive Workload and Musculoskeletal Exposure Modeling for Adaptive Ergonomic Work Design
items.abstract: Cognitive workload, musculoskeletal exposure, fatigue, and limited recovery can jointly affect worker comfort and task performance. However, these factors are often assessed separately, limiting the evaluation of cumulative ergonomic risk over time. This study proposes an integrated ergonomic modeling framework that combines cognitive workload, physical exposure, fatigue accumulation, and recovery within a common assessment structure. Normalized state variables are used to calculate a composite ergonomic risk index, and a proposed multi objective optimization procedure provides a basis for examining alternative task schedules and recovery intervals. Illustrative scenarios compare low, moderate, and high combined demands under specified model assumptions. The proposed analytical design also specifies a procedure for future sensitivity analysis of workload intensity, exposure duration, recovery rate, and worker susceptibility. The illustrative values indicate that higher modeled cognitive workload, physical exposure, and fatigue correspond to greater composite risk under the specified weighting scheme. However, these values are hypothetical and do not represent observed worker data or verified simulation outputs. The framework provides a methodological basis for examining relationships between modeled ergonomic risk and task performance during work schedule planning. Further research should implement reproducible computational experiments, conduct sensitivity analyses, and validate model predictions against measured workload, physical exposure, fatigue, and performance data before practical application.

items.title: Perceived Crisis-Management Training Adequacy and Wellbeing Indicators Among Seafarers During the Red Sea Crisis: An Exploratory Survey
items.abstract: Global shipping carries over 80% of world trade, yet existing supply-chain-resilience theory models resilience at the level of the firm, node and network, without treating the workforce operating those nodes as a variable. This exploratory study addresses that gap using the 2023–2026 Red Sea/Houthi crisis as its empirical setting. A pilot-scale, cross-sectional online survey of 64 serving seafarers combined closed-ended items with qualitative content analysis of two open-text questions. Seafarers who had witnessed or been directly involved in a security incident rated STCW crisis-management training as less adequate for conflict-area risk than those without such exposure (Mann–Whitney U = 227.0, p = 0.007, r = 0.34), the only comparison that remained significant after Holm adjustment within its family of tests; Red Sea transit or Cape of Good Hope rerouting without an incident was not associated with lower ratings. Open-text responses identified situational information and realistic scenario-based drills, rather than generic compliance training, as the specific gap, and a minority questioned seafarers’ right to decline a high-risk voyage. Because fatigue and psychological distress could be captured only through single, non-validated items, findings on these outcomes are indicative only. Building on these results, the study proposes, as exploratory propositions for future testing rather than established relationships, two human-factor pathways through which geopolitical risk may affect operational resilience: a training-competence pathway and a retention/psychological-contract pathway. The study contributes hypothesis-generating evidence, gathered directly from an affected workforce, and derives practical and policy recommendations for STCW training content and seafarer consent protections.

items.title: Revolutionising White‐Collar Help‐Seeking in Organisations: The Impact and Dynamics of Artificial Intelligence‐Driven Chatbots
items.abstract: This study explores how white‐collar workers perceive AI‐driven chatbots, and how affordances and constraints shape their help‐seeking behaviours. Help‐seeking is essential for learning and collaboration but is often limited by social barriers. Drawing on Affordance Theory, this research examines how technological and social affordances influence chatbot use. Based on 24 in‐depth interviews, conducted between May and December 2023, at the inception of ChatGPT's public diffusion, the study reveals that chatbots offer judgement‐free support for repetitive and informational tasks, fostering autonomy and bypassing interpersonal discomfort. However, concerns about trust, limited capabilities, surveillance and job security constrain adoption. Individual mindset and age, together with organisational culture (e.g., innovation climate), further influence use. Chatbots redefine help‐seeking as a human‐machine dynamic, complementing rather than replacing human support. The study highlights the importance of designing chatbot systems that align with user needs and workplace cultures. In doing so, it contributes to debates on algorithmic management and worker autonomy and offers practical implications for integrating AI tools to support knowledge sharing and collaboration in work environments.

items.title: xLightGCN: Explainable Graph Neural Network Based Recommendation Systems with Most Influential Peers
items.abstract: Recommendation systems, systems that predict a user's preference for items in order to curate that user's feed, are a ubiquitous and central feature in online social networks. While they are a central piece of our modern digital infrastructure, many modern approaches are opaque black boxes, making them difficult to audit, understand, and assess the trustworthiness of. In this paper we present an exact, graph-based approach for generating explanations for decisions made by recommendation systems. We argue that in the risk-sensitive sociotechnical context of user-facing AI such as recommendation systems, explainability is a key pillar for establishing the trustworthiness of models and validating their effectiveness. We propose a technique built on LightGCN-like architectures, an influential and popular class of recommendation models. We describe our approach and argue that it provides an appropriate assurance mechanism for these AI systems leading to specific advantages, including interpretable explanations and a theoretically guaranteed measure of explanation fidelity. We conclude by discussing limitations and directions for future research.

items.title: Mapping the Neural-Behavioral-Psychological Link: An fNIRS Study on Driver Trust and Intervention in Perception-Gap Scenarios
items.abstract: V2X-enabled automated vehicles navigating obstructed hazards create a human-system “perception gap,” potentially triggering unsafe driver interventions. This study examined the prefrontal neural correlates of intervention and trust during simulated perception-gap scenarios. We analyzed 231 trials from 31 drivers navigating 8 obstructed hazards under partial automation. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) features across six frontotemporal regions were evaluated using generalized estimating equations. Behaviorally, higher trust predicted lower intervention probability. Neurally, results revealed a timing–amplitude dissociation: prolonged hemodynamic timings correlated with lower intervention odds and higher trust. Conversely, amplified HbR troughs and higher mean HbO/HbT activity predicted higher intervention odds, while lower HbR trough amplitudes aligned with higher trust. These neurophysiological insights offer a foundation for adaptive human-machine interfaces designed to dynamically calibrate trust and mitigate unwarranted takeovers.

items.title: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies
items.abstract: Language-generating AI systems are no longer only objects of linguistic interaction: their outputs increasingly re-enter the communicative and institutional practices from which their training material was drawn. Drawing on social theory, social epistemology, and the philosophy of language, this article develops a sociotechnical account of that re-entry. We introduce recursive semantic normalization: the process through which machine-generated formulations, once recurrently taken up, evaluated, reused, and institutionally retained, participate in the reproduction and transformation of semantic regularities. Under the heading of technohybridism, we argue that the relevant unit of analysis is the hybrid semantic system, a recursively coupled configuration of human practices, computational generation, and institutional uptake. First, we distinguish the concept from neighbouring accounts, including model collapse, looping effects, machine habitus, machine culture, and the epistemology of AI testimony. Second, we develop an analytical model that separates generation, selection, uptake, and persistence and distinguishes machine-attributable change from change that would have occurred anyway. Third, we analyse uptake as routinized, institutionally diffused, and socially stratified practice and state conditions under which machine-derived regularities become norms. Fourth, we identify social-epistemic consequences: the laundering of provenance that weakens epistemic vigilance, the erosion of the cognitive diversity on which collective inquiry depends, and the narrowing of shared hermeneutical resources. An evidential ladder for empirical research follows. The account attributes no normative authority to machine outputs; what changes is the field within which human and institutional uptake operates.

items.title: ENGLISH EDUCATION STUDENTS’ PERCEPTIONS OF USING AI TOOLS IN ACADEMIC WRITING: A CASE STUDY
items.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly altered academic writing practices in higher education, yet its pedagogical implications for pre-service English teachers remain underexplored. This qualitative case study aimed to investigate English Education students' perceptions of utilizing AI tools in academic writing, specifically examining perceived benefits, operational challenges, and academic integrity negotiations. Ten undergraduate students, comprising eight eighth-semester and two sixth-semester students at Institut Pendidikan Indonesia, were purposively recruited. Data were gathered through an asynchronous online open-ended questionnaire and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis framework. The findings revealed that students utilized AI tools primarily for brainstorming, outlining, and grammatical refinement, while contending with fabricated citations, stylistic rigidity, and anxieties regarding the erosion of independent critical thinking. In negotiating academic integrity, participants practiced selective verification and established a collective ethical boundary that endorsed linguistic scaffolding while strictly proscribing unreflective wholesale text generation. ABSTRAK Integrasi kecerdasan buatan generatif (generative artificial intelligence) telah merevolusi praktik penulisan akademik di perguruan tinggi, namun pemaknaan pedagogis oleh mahasiswa calon guru bahasa Inggris masih jarang diteliti secara mendalam. Penelitian studi kasus kualitatif ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi persepsi mahasiswa Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris terhadap penggunaan perangkat kecerdasan buatan (AI tools) dalam penulisan akademik, yang berfokus pada persepsi manfaat, tantangan, dan negosiasi integritas akademik. Sebanyak sepuluh mahasiswa sarjana yang terdiri atas delapan mahasiswa Semester 8 dan dua mahasiswa Semester 6 di Institut Pendidikan Indonesia dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dihimpun melalui kuesioner terbuka daring asinkron (asynchronous open-ended questionnaire) dan dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik enam tahap. Hasil penelitian mengungkapkan bahwa mahasiswa memanfaatkan perangkat kecerdasan buatan terutama untuk pencarian ide awal, penyusunan kerangka karangan, serta perbaikan tata bahasa, meskipun mereka menghadapi kendala berupa sitasi halusinasi, kekakuan gaya bahasa, dan kecemasan akan erosi keterampilan berpikir kritis mandiri. Dalam menegosiasikan integritas akademik, mahasiswa menerapkan adopsi selektif dengan memverifikasi rujukan ilmiah serta menyepakati batasan etis bahwa bantuan penyuntingan bahasa dapat dibenarkan, sedangkan penyalinan teks secara utuh merupakan bentuk pelanggaran.

items.title: ENGLISH TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS OF GENERATIVE AI USE IN TEACHING WRITING
items.abstract: This study aims to explore English teachers’ perceptions regarding the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in teaching writing at the senior high school level. A qualitative descriptive case study design was employed at a public senior high school in Garut, West Java. The participants were two experienced English teachers purposively selected based on their teaching tenure and digital tool integration. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews, pedagogical document analysis, and observational field notes, then examined using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis. The analysis yielded six core themes: GenAI as a support for student writing, GenAI as a support for teaching, GenAI as a risk to independent learning, GenAI as a risk to textual authenticity, GenAI as a tool demanding responsible use, and GenAI as a challenge for writing assessment. The findings demonstrate that teachers maintain a conditional and context-dependent perception of AI integration. While teachers recognize its utility for lexical scaffolding and conceptual brainstorming, they emphasize rigorous boundary setting to prevent the erosion of learner autonomy and textual originality. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi persepsi guru bahasa Inggris terhadap pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) dalam pembelajaran menulis pada jenjang sekolah menengah atas. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus deskriptif pada sebuah SMA negeri di Garut, Jawa Barat. Partisipan terdiri atas dua orang guru bahasa Inggris berpengalaman yang dipilih secara purposif berdasarkan kriteria masa kerja dan kebiasaan memanfaatkan teknologi digital. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, analisis artefak pembelajaran, dan catatan lapangan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik model enam tahap Braun dan Clarke. Hasil analisis menghasilkan enam tema utama: GenAI sebagai pendukung tulisan siswa, GenAI sebagai pendukung pengajaran, GenAI sebagai risiko terhadap pembelajaran mandiri siswa, GenAI sebagai risiko terhadap keaslian tulisan, GenAI sebagai alat yang memerlukan penggunaan bertanggung jawab, dan GenAI sebagai tantangan bagi asesmen menulis. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa persepsi guru bersifat kondisional dan terikat pada konteks pedagogis di ruang kelas. Guru memandang GenAI bermanfaat untuk stimulasi kosakata dan ide awal, namun penggunaannya harus dibatasi agar tidak mengikis kemandirian berpikir serta orisinalitas karya tulis siswa.

items.abstract: Educational assessment at the elementary level extends beyond measuring the extent to which instructional objectives have been achieved, as it also influences students’ perceptions of their own abilities, the quality of classroom participation, and their motivation to continue learning. The present article aims to explain the role of modern assessment models in enhancing learning motivation among elementary school students and to identify the psychological and educational mechanisms underlying this relationship. This study employs a descriptive-analytical approach based on library research and a review of relevant scholarly articles. The analysis examines the characteristics of descriptive assessment, formative assessment, performance-based assessment, self-assessment, peer assessment, and portfolio assessment, with particular emphasis on constructive feedback, active participation, and attention to individual progress. Findings derived from the reviewed literature indicate that replacing exclusively grade-centered judgment with clear and process-oriented feedback can strengthen students’ sense of competence, academic self-efficacy, responsibility, and intrinsic motivation. Furthermore, opportunities to correct errors, awareness of one’s progress, and reduced pressure resulting from comparisons among students can promote more informed and active participation in learning activities. The effectiveness of these assessment models depends on teachers’ ability to establish clear criteria, accommodate individual differences, and involve families in the educational process. Accordingly, modern assessment can become a source of motivation when it is integrated continuously into the teaching process, thereby making the learning experience more meaningful.

items.title: PERAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DAN INFRASTRUKTUR DIGITAL DALAM MENINGKATKAN KETERLIBATAN AKADEMIK DAN EFEKTIVITAS BELAJAR MAHASISWA
items.abstract: The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into higher education has created new opportunities to support the learning process. However, the effectiveness of technology utilization is not solely determined by technical availability, but also by students' active involvement in learning activities. This study aims to analyze the role of AI utilization and digital infrastructure in enhancing learning effectiveness, with student engagement serving as a mediating variable among students at Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. A quantitative survey approach was administered to 347 active students across faculties and cohorts selected through multistage stratified sampling. Data were gathered using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with a second-order construct through the Hierarchical Component Model. The results demonstrate that AI usage and digital infrastructure exert positive and significant effects on student engagement and learning effectiveness. Furthermore, student engagement partially mediates the effects of AI usage and digital infrastructure on learning effectiveness, with AI usage exhibiting a more dominant total contribution. ABSTRAK Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan teknologi digital telah memberikan peluang baru dalam mendukung proses pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi. Namun, efektivitas pemanfaatan teknologi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh ketersediaan fasilitas semata, melainkan juga oleh keterlibatan aktif mahasiswa dalam proses akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran pemanfaatan AI dan infrastruktur digital dalam meningkatkan efektivitas belajar dengan keterlibatan mahasiswa (student engagement) sebagai variabel mediasi pada mahasiswa Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei diterapkan kepada 347 mahasiswa aktif dari berbagai fakultas dan angkatan yang dipilih melalui teknik multistage stratified sampling. Pengumpulan data menggunakan kuesioner skala Likert lima tingkat dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan model konstruk tingkat kedua melalui Hierarchical Component Model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keterlibatan mahasiswa serta efektivitas belajar. Selain itu, keterlibatan mahasiswa terbukti memediasi secara parsial pengaruh penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital terhadap efektivitas belajar, dengan pemanfaatan AI memberikan kontribusi total yang lebih dominan.

items.title: Responsible AI in Academic Research: A Systematic Review of Ethical Principles, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is now present in every stage of the academic research life cycle, yet the rules governing its use remain fragmented. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review used 34 structured search strings and citation chasing to search literature published between 2015 and 2025. Of 359 records identified, 124 studies and documents met the inclusion criteria: 40 empirical studies, 43 conceptual analyses or commentaries, 20 policy and guidance documents, 17 reviews and 4 methodological frameworks; 83% were published from 2023 onwards. Guidance converges on a narrow set of standards: AI cannot be an author, material use must be disclosed, and humans remain accountable. Disclosure thresholds, AI in peer review, AI-generated images, AI-text detectors and the regulatory treatment of research remain contested. Challenges fall into three clusters: algorithmic bias; data governance, privacy and consent; and transparency, reproducibility and integrity, where empirical studies document fabricated references, unreliable and biased detectors, and rapidly rising, mostly undisclosed AI use. Emerging responses include lifecycle-based guidance, structured documentation, tailored ethics review and interdisciplinary oversight. We propose an integrated framework linking five principles to five research stages and an agenda emphasizing context-sensitive ethics, public participation and international coordination.

items.title: Trust in AI Clinical Decision Support Systems: A Scoping Review of Measurement and Behavior
items.abstract: Abstract Trust in artificial intelligence clinical decision support systems is critical to appropriate reliance, yet its measurement and behavioral implications remain unclear. We conducted a scoping review of quantitative studies published between January 2010 and June 2026, searching PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase. Thirty-three studies met inclusion criteria. Fourteen (42.4%) explicitly defined trust, and 16 (48.5%) assessed anticipated or hypothetical trust without direct system interaction. Twenty-seven studies (81.8%) examined factors associated with trust, emphasizing human–AI interaction and system characteristics over organizational and social contexts. Trust patterns varied across healthcare professionals, patients, and general populations, although direct comparisons were rare. Twenty-seven studies assessed separate AI-related behavioral outcomes, but only 11 formally tested trust–behavior relationships. Reported trust did not consistently correspond to preferences or decisions when AI and clinician recommendations conflicted. More comparable measures and observed behavioral outcomes are needed to evaluate appropriately calibrated trust in clinical AI.

items.title: A Critical Analysis of AI from the Perspective of the Philosophy of Science among Grade X Students at SMA Don Bosco Padang
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates access to information in education, increasing the importance of critically evaluating claims and their underlying assumptions. This study examined Grade 10 students’ ability to distinguish facts, opinions, and values in AI-related information at SMA Don Bosco Padang from a philosophy of science perspective. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed involving 33 students. Data were collected through a 15-item written test comprising five items each for fact, opinion, and value identification. Descriptive analysis examined frequencies, percentages of correct responses, score distributions, and classification error patterns. Across 495 responses, 337 were correct and 158 were incorrect, yielding an overall accuracy of 68.08%. Accuracy was highest for opinion identification (76.36%), followed by fact identification (67.88%) and value identification (60.00%). Value identification presented the greatest difficulty, with an error rate of 40.00%. These findings reveal descriptive differences in students’ classification performance, particularly their greater difficulty recognizing values within AI-related information. From a philosophy of science perspective, the results underscore the relevance of epistemology for evaluating evidence and the justification of claims, alongside axiology for recognizing ethical considerations. The study provides contextual evidence to inform AI literacy instruction that integrates information verification, critical reasoning, and ethical reflection to support responsible technology use.

items.title: A Data Engineering-Driven Machine Learning Framework for EFL Writing Performance Analysis
items.abstract: Explainable machine learning has been applied to textual predictors of writing quality, but rarely to the behavioral and motivational predictors, feedback modality and self-regulated learning (SRL), that dominate confirmatory EFL writing research. This study analyzes a quasi-experimental, ten-week EFL writing-feedback intervention (n=84), recording feedback condition (instructor-mediated, automated, or generative-AI), proficiency, and 35-item SRL strategy use alongside pre/post analytic writing scores across six outcomes. A pre-modeling reliability check found the SRL questionnaire did not reproduce its published factor structure (Cronbach's alpha = 0.279), so a single composite served as the motivational predictor, with centered feedback-by-SRL interaction terms. Five model classes were compared under nested cross-validation with per-trait tuning. Random forest achieved the best aggregate performance (MCRMSE = 2.240, mean R² = 0.293); a stacked ensemble performed worse than its base learners on every trait (mean R² = −0.344). A fixed-hyperparameter baseline outperformed the nested-CV-tuned pipeline (MCRMSE 2.197 vs. 2.258), showing tuning, not feature engineering, degraded performance here. SHAP attribution identified feedback condition, especially generative-AI feedback, as the dominant predictor for all six outcomes, with feedback-by-SRL interactions outweighing SRL's own main effect on three of six traits. A multi-task neural network outperformed an equivalent single-task ensemble on every trait using 5.75 times fewer parameters. These results show explainable, cross-validated machine learning can corroborate confirmatory EFL writing findings while surfacing measurement and methodological cautions.

items.title: A Digital Ergonomics Framework for Preventive Workstation and Work-Process Optimization Using OWAS-Based Risk Assessment
items.abstract: Ergonomic workstation design is essential for improving the fit between workers, tasks, and the work environment while reducing the risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders. The Ovako Working Posture Analysis System (OWAS) is widely used for ergonomic risk assessment; however, its conventional application to dynamic work can be inefficient because numerous working postures must be observed and evaluated. Moreover, conventional ergonomic design often requires multiple physical mock-ups, while motion-capture technologies such as Kinect are generally applied to existing work conditions, limiting their use for preventive evaluation during the design stage. This study proposes a digital ergonomics framework integrating workstation modeling, work-process simulation, and OWAS-based risk assessment for preventive ergonomic optimization. Digital models of the workstation and work activities were developed to simulate worker postures and identify potentially hazardous conditions before physical implementation. OWAS was used to classify postural risks and determine the required corrective actions. Workstation configurations and work procedures associated with higher risk levels were iteratively modified and reassessed in the digital environment. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can identify and reduce ergonomic risks during the design stage without extensive physical prototyping. Higher-risk postures were mitigated through iterative modifications of workstation configurations and work procedures. This framework provides a systematic preventive approach for integrating ergonomic assessment into workstation and work-process design, supporting safer working conditions while improving the efficiency of the ergonomic design process

items.title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
items.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

items.title: A systematic review of research issues with Levels of Automation (LOA)
items.abstract: This systematic review critically analyzes the contexts and challenges of Levels of Automation (LOA), particularly in light of advancements by Artificial Intelligence (AI). Human–automation interaction (HAI) seeks to understand how humans interact with automated systems, particularly as increasing automation places operators increasingly out of the loop. A foundational framework within this field is the Levels of Automation (LOA) framework, which characterizes the respective roles and capabilities of human operators and automated systems. As AI becomes increasingly integrated into traditional HAI applications, a renewed examination of the current state of LOA is warranted. This systematic review examines the following research question: What research demographics, contexts, and challenges associated with LOA are reported in the literature? Data analysis, extraction, and open and axial coding were employed, and consensus was reached by iterative discussion between the authors. The review ultimately included 118 studies. The review identified six contextual categories and 26 challenge codes. The findings provide a comprehensive analysis of the evolving landscape of human–automation interaction. The contribution of this work is to outline weaknesses embedded in research with LOA and suggest a reform with prospects of enhanced HAI with AI.

items.title: A Systematic Review: The Conditions Shaping GenAI's Impact on Iranian Education
items.abstract: This systematic review synthesizes 15 empirical studies published in 2026 to examine how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is affecting Iranian education and what the current evidence supports. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a search of four databases yielded 710 records, of which 15 empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in a thematic synthesis. The corpus comprises twelve journal articles and three chapters in edited volumes. The synthesis identified four themes. The first is that GenAI is effective when it is paired with human mediation and less effective when it replaces it, a finding that is replicated across every study in the corpus that compared AI-only and hybrid conditions. The second is that the benefits of GenAI are unevenly distributed across linguistic domains, with stronger effects on fluency, complexity, and self-efficacy than on accuracy or global proficiency. The third is an affective asymmetry, in which learners gain in enjoyment, well-being, and self-efficacy while teachers bear new costs in the form of AI-induced anxiety and monitoring workload. The fourth is a gap between individual adoption and institutional readiness, in which teachers and students are willing to use AI while the institutional structures that would make this use sustainable have not been built. The review argues that the positive impacts reported in the literature are real but conditional, produced in designed settings that most Iranian institutions have not yet created, and that closing this gap requires hybrid models of instruction, localized tools, AI literacy training that addresses the affective dimensions of adoption, and policy frameworks suited to under-resourced higher education.

items.title: AI Adoption at Higher Education Institutions: A Call for Designated AI Management
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming teaching, learning and administration in higher education institutions (HEIs), yet responsibility for its governance is rarely assigned. This article develops and empirically tests the profile of an AI Manager for HEIs proposed by the Erasmus+ project FORCE AI. A literature-based definition and nine-area competence profile were examined in a sequential mixed-methods study, a survey of 387 students and staff from 13 countries and five nominal-group focus groups in Germany, Latvia, the Netherlands, and Türkiye in 2025, which tested the elements stakeholders can rate: competences, responsibilities, placement, and qualifications. Only 17% of respondents knew of a designated AI-management responsibility at their institution; of the remainder, 71% considered one necessary and 76% expected an AI Manager to improve their experience. The expected mandate comprised training, ethical oversight, data security and strategy; preferences were split between a dedicated position and a shared cross-functional function. Survey respondents portrayed the role as a compliance-oriented technical specialist, whereas staff-dominated focus groups, rating the same competencies, prioritised leadership, change and project management, and communication alongside AI expertise and ethics; this contrast between methods and samples persists for staff respondents alone. The revised definition and profile position designated AI management, a dedicated AI Manager or a team with an accountable lead, as change leadership with technical credibility and give HEIs a tested basis for establishing this role.

items.title: AI as a Thinking Partner in Sustainability-Oriented Mathematical Modelling: An Exploratory Study of Pre-Service Teachers’ Comparative Reflection
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is mostly used in education to generate solutions, provide feedback or support instruction; approaches that use AI outputs as objects of comparison and reflection remain less explored. This small-scale exploratory qualitative case study examined AI-supported comparative reflection in sustainability-oriented mathematical modelling. Twelve pre-service mathematics teachers individually developed models for a task on water use in a school garden and then compared them with a model produced by ChatGPT (GPT-4o), reflecting on the comparison in writing. Modelling products, written comparisons and reflection forms were analysed using inductive content analysis. The comparison prompted participants to question assumptions, identify limitations in both models and consider alternative variables and representations; most described how they would revise their models. Their accounts contained indications of critical, creative and metacognitive reasoning. However, several participants treated the AI output as an answer key, some of their critiques echoed weaknesses that the AI had listed about itself, and none noticed a computational inconsistency deliberately retained in the output. As the design included no comparison condition or pre–post measure, the findings describe patterns of reasoning displayed during the activity, not improvements in thinking skills or modelling competence. Implications for teacher education are discussed.

items.title: AI as assistant, not creative co-author: AI imaginaries among Social Cartoon Influencers in Vietnam
items.abstract: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) have intensified debates about automation, authorship, and labour across creative industries. Yet these discussions are often dominated by disruption and replacement narratives, leaving limited attention to how creators interpret and negotiate AI in everyday practice, particularly in non-Western contexts. This paper examines how Social Cartoon Influencers (SCIs) in Vietnam interpret and use GenAI within their routine creative production. The study combines semi-structured interviews and contextual observations of production workflows through the lens of AI imaginaries. Findings reveal that creators position AI as a creative assistant rather than a co-author, using it for ideation, optimisation and routine tasks, while reserving final authorship for humans. The clear human-AI boundary results from concerns surrounding situated notions of authenticity and ‘national tone’. The paper argues that AI adoption is shaped by negotiated boundaries around authorship, authenticity, and cultural legitimacy.

items.title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

items.title: AI Literacy and AI Anxiety as Differential Correlates of Positive and Negative Attitudes Towards Artificial Intelligence Among Speech and Language Therapists in Türkiye
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied in speech and language therapy (SLT). Evidence on SLTs’ attitudes towards it has been largely descriptive, generated with study-specific questionnaires or with validated attitude scales analysed descriptively. The psychological factors associated with those attitudes have recently been examined among undergraduate students in the profession, but not among clinicians in practice. Aims: To examine whether AI literacy and AI anxiety are independently associated with attitudes towards AI beyond prior AI use, self-directed AI learning and formal AI training, and whether the two are differentially related to the positive and negative dimensions of those attitudes. Methods & Procedures: A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 180 SLTs in Türkiye, recruited by convenience and predominantly early in their careers (mean age 25.4 years), using the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale, the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale and the General Attitudes towards Artificial Intelligence Scale (GAAIS). Hierarchical multiple regressions were complemented by comparisons of each construct’s correlations and adjusted coefficients across the two attitude dimensions, sensitivity analyses and post hoc confirmatory factor analyses. Outcomes & Results: Beyond the experiential variables, AI literacy and AI anxiety explained an additional 15.2% of the variance in positive attitudes, with AI literacy the only independent correlate (β = .403, p < .001), and an additional 42.1% of the variance in attitudes towards AI-related drawbacks (reverse-scored, so that higher values indicate fewer concerns), with anxiety the only independent correlate (β = −.679, p < .001). Each construct was significantly more strongly associated with one dimension than with the other, in both zero-order correlations and adjusted coefficients (all p ≤ .001). None of the AI-related experiential variables remained significant. The pattern held across sensitivity analyses, in which one year or more of professional experience was also associated with more positive attitudes. Absolute fit was poor for the GAAIS and AI literacy measurement models and mixed for the AI anxiety model. Conclusions & Implications: In a predominantly early-career, private-sector sample of Turkish SLTs, self-reported AI literacy and AI anxiety were differentially associated with attitudes towards AI, each related primarily to a different attitude dimension. These patterns require cautious interpretation, because the anxiety and negative-attitude measures, although empirically distinguishable, share item content and substantial variance, and because the literacy measure indexes general rather than clinically situated competence. AI literacy and AI-related concerns may still be complementary targets for education supporting clinically responsible integration of AI into SLT.

items.title: An Impactal study on Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) in the Context of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) have substantially influenced artificial intelligence by enabling computational systems to learn representations from images, language, behavioural sequences, and other complex data. This paper presents a selective narrative review of their conceptual development, applications, evaluation requirements, and societal implications. It synthesises foundational and application-oriented publications concerning computer vision, natural language processing, healthcare image classification, financial prediction, cybersecurity, and reinforcement learning. The review uses a qualitative comparative framework to examine the task addressed, the evidence reported, and the conditions limiting interpretation. The reviewed literature illustrates the value of learned representations and task-specific architectures, while also showing why benchmark performance cannot alone establish operational reliability or social benefit. Cross-cutting concerns include data quality, distribution shift, interpretability, subgroup disparities, adversarial vulnerability, privacy, and computational requirements. The paper proposes a practical evaluation framework connecting task suitability, data provenance, appropriate baselines, external validation, human oversight, and monitoring after deployment. No new model training, expert interviews, public-opinion survey, or pooled statistical analysis is reported. The synthesis concludes that the contribution of ANNs should be assessed through performance under relevant operating conditions and the consequences of their use, rather than through accuracy alone. Keywords: artificial neural networks; artificial intelligence; deep learning; representation learning; model evaluation; responsible AI.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Integration in Education: Teachers’ Utilization, Perceptions, and Implementation Challenges
items.abstract: This study explored the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in chemistry instruction, focusing on teachers’ utilization patterns, perceptions, and the challenges they encounter. A sample of 18 chemistry teachers from various institutions participated, providing insights into the types and frequency of AI tools used, including ChatGPT, ChemCollective, and PhET Interactive Simulations. Findings indicate that generative AI tools—particularly ChatGPT—are the most widely adopted due to their accessibility, versatility, and ease of integration. In contrast, subject-specific and creative AI platforms remain underutilized, suggesting that familiarity, perceived complexity, and awareness significantly influence adoption patterns. Teachers demonstrated strongly positive perceptions of AI integration in both curriculum and instruction, recognizing its potential to enhance content delivery, student engagement, personalized learning, and the development of 21st-century skills. No significant differences were found across institutions, indicating a shared readiness to integrate AI in chemistry education. Despite these favorable perceptions, effective implementation is constrained by technical limitations, infrastructure gaps, data quality concerns, usability challenges, ethical issues, and privacy risks. Teachers also expressed concerns about over-reliance on AI and the potential reduction of meaningful teacher–student interaction, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a balanced, human-centered approach. Overall, the findings support the strategic and guided adoption of AI as a pedagogical enhancement tool rather than a substitute for professional judgment and instructional expertise. The results highlight the need for structured, discipline-specific professional development that emphasizes prompt literacy, critical evaluation of AI outputs, ethical awareness, and pedagogical alignment. Strengthening technological infrastructure, establishing sustained institutional support systems, and developing clear guidelines for responsible AI use are essential to ensure effective, equitable, and ethically grounded integration of AI in chemistry education.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and the erosion of professional autonomy in clinical practice – a review and analysis
items.abstract: Professional autonomy is a foundational ethical principle in healthcare, underpinning healthcare professionals’ capacity to exercise independent clinical judgement in light of a patient's particular circumstances, preferences and needs. While ethical debate surrounding medical AI has focused extensively on safety, accuracy and bias, its implications for professional autonomy have received comparatively less attention, a notable omission given AI's growing role in shaping clinical decision-making. This article identifies three salient mechanisms through which AI integration may constrain professional autonomy: (1) algorithmic opacity and explainability, (2) automation bias and de-skilling and (3) institutional pressures. Whilst proposed safeguards such as explainable AI, professional training, system design and institutional governance represent important directions, they do not yet adequately protect professional autonomy. This article therefore calls for closer scrutiny of current approaches to AI integration and for governance frameworks that attend not only to the technical properties of AI systems, but to the organisational and institutional conditions in which they are deployed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Youth Development: Assessing Negative Impacts in Cameroon
items.abstract: This research evaluates the negative impacts of Artificial Intelligence dependency on the cognitive and academic development of students within the Cameroonian higher education landscape. Utilizing a multiple case study design to facilitate literal replication across diverse settings, this study analyzed data collected from students at the University of Yaoundé, the University of Bamenda, and Yaoundé International Business School. A total of 525 students were surveyed using a purposive sampling strategy to account for the unique dynamics of public university massification and private sector specialization in Cameroon. The findings indicate a high prevalence of AI utilization, with 85.3% of respondents reporting daily or weekly usage for academic tasks.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR STRATEGIC DECISION-MAKING: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE TRANSFORMATION OF BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
items.abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving business environment, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a transformative technological capability with profound implications for strategic decision-making and modern business management. The growing ability of AI systems to analyse extensive volumes of structured and unstructured data, detect intricate patterns, produce predictive insights, and automate analytical activities is reshaping the processes through which organisations formulate and implement strategic decisions. Through the review of recent literature and real-world case studies, this paper critically argues that AI is fundamentally reshaping strategic decision-making and presents a reasoned perspective on how this shift is transforming business management practices and competitive strategies in contemporary organisations. This study also explores the challenges and risks of AI-driven strategic decision-making. The study concludes that the greatest value of AI lies in its capacity to augment rather than replace managerial intelligence. Hence, the study recommends that organisations should adopt hybrid decision-making by combining AI-generated insights with human expertise to enhance decision accuracy, critical thinking, and strategic judgement.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION THROUGH THE FOUNDATIONS OF BASIC RESEARCH, ECOLOGY AND ACADEMIC CONSCIENCE: A REFLECTIVE COMMENTARY
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly discussed through frameworks of adoption, automation, and organisational reinvention. Their application to higher education requires careful consideration of what education is intended to achieve. This reflective commentary examines McKinsey's three horizons of AI transformation through my experiences in ecological research, university teaching, postgraduate supervision, and academic writing. It develops ten connected arguments concerning scientific foundations, independent learning, field experience, curiosity, institutional resilience, academic conscience, respectful leadership, educational relationships, environmental responsibility, and selective adoption. Selected empirical studies and foundational ecological literature support the discussion, while personal judgments are distinguished from established findings. I argue that faster production of academic material alone cannot demonstrate deeper understanding or stronger research competence. AI can help when its use aligns with learning objectives and is supported by verification, fair assessment, and accountable human decisions. Risks include dependence on generated explanations, weakening of observational skills, restriction of exploratory inquiry, unfair judgments about authorship, increased workload, unequal access, and environmental costs. An ecological perspective also encourages attention to relationships, feedback, and institutions' ability to function when technological services fail. I propose that universities assess AI by what students can explain independently, how reliably they engage with evidence, and the quality of educational relationships. The central responsibility is to preserve the conditions that enable people to become capable researchers and conscientious members of society.

items.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe integration of artificial intelligence (AI) has profoundly transformed human resource management (HRM) from an administrative function into a strategic decision-making process, creating a critical need to balance algorithmic effectiveness with operational challenges. The purpose of this study is to explore the evolving integration of artificial intelligence within human resource management. This paper utilizes a bibliometric analysis using PRISMA reporting flow guidelines, analyzing data retrieved from the Scopus database for the period from 2015 to 2025. The results reveal an exponential expansion of scientific research over the decade. Out of an initial set of 2,949 publications, 622 relevant documents met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using VOSviewer. Annual publications grew from nine articles in 2015 to 218 articles in 2025. The geographical distribution shows that India leads the field with 116 publications, followed by China (114) and the United States (98). Furthermore, the thematic mapping identifies nine distinct clusters, with AI and human resource management standing out as the primary domains experiencing transformation. The findings confirm that the field has become a consolidated, dynamic discipline, with strategic implications for organizations seeking to align technological efficiency with organizational justice, ethical considerations, and employee well-being.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in radiology education: from AI-supported learning to clinical innovation—a narrative review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing diagnostic radiology, but education and training have not kept pace. This narrative review brings together current evidence on AI-supported learning in radiology education and how such learning can move into clinical innovation. Surveys from different countries point to the same gap: in a 25-country international survey of radiographers, radiologists, and students, only 10.3% had received formal AI training; in one national survey of Turkish residents, 84.5% had received none. The review maps competency frameworks and curriculum models that define AI literacy and support staged integration into residency. It also assesses AI as a teaching tool, including AI-assisted case-based learning, computer-aided diagnosis training, precision-education knowledge recommenders, and virtual, augmented, and extended reality. Controlled and randomized studies show measurable gains: computer-aided diagnosis training raised resident scores above self-study controls (mean score 52 vs. 38 on a 100-point scale), while an AI-based knowledge recommender shortened reporting time by 162 s per case and relative improvement in graded reporting accuracy scores of 14% (95% CI 8.1–19.8%). Large language models are promising but limited: GPT-4 approaches board-style examination performance (80.6%) yet remains poor at image-based reasoning (47.8%). The review closes by considering how education can feed clinical innovation, along with algorithmic and automation bias, ethical governance, and future research needs. AI education should therefore span the full continuum-from undergraduate training to continuing professional development-if radiology is to innovate safely, effectively, and equitably.

items.title: Artificial intelligence readiness in healthcare and health professions education in conflict-affected Syria: an online cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly relevant to healthcare delivery, clinical training, and health professions education. Evidence from conflict-affected settings remains limited, despite workforce shortages, disrupted training pathways, and constrained digital infrastructure. This study assessed AI knowledge, trust, willingness, and digital capability among Syrian adults and healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals), with emphasis on implications for AI literacy and professional education. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of Syrian adults from March 4th to May 31st 2026, using a 35-item questionnaire distributed via social media through convenience sampling. The survey assessed AI awareness, trust, willingness, perceived risks and benefits, barriers to healthcare and digital health use, and Digital Literacy. Healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals) completed additional items on clinical AI use and exposure to unsafe AI recommendations. Composite scores were calculated for AI Trust (3–15), AI Willingness (4–20), and Digital Literacy (2–10). Internal consistency was acceptable to excellent across scales (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.787–0.856). Among 829 participants, 353 (42.6%) were healthcare respondents (119 students and 234 qualified professionals). Mean AI Willingness, AI Trust, and Digital Literacy scores were 14.5 (SD 3.25), 11.0 (SD 2.34), and 6.67 (SD 1.80), respectively. In multivariable linear regression, AI Trust (β = 0.483) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.305) were the strongest predictors, followed by General AI Knowledge (β = 0.165). In sensitivity models excluding the Willingness item that loaded on Trust, Trust (β = 0.44 and 0.38) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.31 and 0.33) remained the strongest correlates. Educational use was the most accepted AI application (65.5%) and educational support was the leading perceived benefit (64.2%). Medical errors were the most frequently perceived risk (76.6%), while cost, unreliable internet access, and lack of Arabic-language content were major implementation barriers. In this online convenience sample, Trust and Digital Literacy were the strongest independent correlates of Willingness to use AI, followed by AI knowledge. The high acceptance of educational AI suggests a practical entry point for conflict-affected health systems. AI literacy should be integrated into undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing health professions education, with explicit training on critical appraisal, safe use, bias, privacy, local validation, and clinician oversight.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Auditor Trust, and Fraud Detection in FinTech Audits: Evidence from Iraq
items.abstract: FinTech has shifted financial activity towards platforms that generate high-volume, high-velocity transaction data, creating new opportunities for fraud. This study examines the association between AI-enabled auditing and auditors' perceived fraud-detection effectiveness in FinTech environments, and whether this association varies with auditors' trust in AI tools. Drawing on trust-in-automation and technology acceptance research, we surveyed 214 auditors engaged with Iraqi banks and licensed electronic payment providers and tested the hypotheses using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped moderation analysis. The results show a positive association between AI-enabled auditing and perceived fraud-detection effectiveness. Auditor trust in AI has no statistically significant direct association with detection effectiveness, but it positively moderates the association between AI-enabled auditing and fraud detection: the estimated association is approximately 2.6 times stronger among high-trust auditors than among low-trust auditors. Trust therefore appears to act as a moderating condition rather than an independent predictor of perceived detection effectiveness. The study extends the discussion of audit technology beyond adoption to consider how trust conditions its perceived effectiveness. It also provides evidence from an emerging FinTech market in which research remains limited. For regulators, audit firms and FinTech supervisors, the findings suggest the importance of calibrated rather than uncritical trust in AI, supported by explainable tools, targeted training and clear guidance on AI-generated audit evidence.

items.title: Attitudes towards artificial intelligence and their association with innovative behaviour among diploma nursing students in selected state nursing training schools in Sri Lanka: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare and education. Nursing students will enter AI-enabled clinical environments, yet evidence from Sri Lanka on their attitudes towards AI and how these relate to innovative behaviour is limited. This study assessed AI attitudes and innovative behaviour and examined their association among diploma nursing students in selected state nursing training schools in Sri Lanka. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 282 diploma nursing students from Kalutara and Galle Nursing Training Schools using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using an expert-reviewed and pretested self-administered questionnaire comprising sociodemographic items, the 13-item Artificial Intelligence Attitude Scale, and the 10-item Innovative Work Behaviour Scale. Descriptive statistics and tests of normality were performed in IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Because the total scores were not normally distributed, Spearman's rank-order correlation was used to examine the association between AI attitudes and innovative behaviour. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Among 282 participants, 228 (80.9%) were female and 260 (92.2%) were third-year students. The mean AI attitude score was 44.32 (SD 4.65), and the mean innovative behaviour score was 35.73 (SD 4.79). AI attitude scores showed a weak but statistically significant positive correlation with innovative behaviour scores (Spearman's rho = 0.203, p < 0.001). Conclusions More favourable AI attitudes were associated with slightly higher innovative behaviour among diploma nursing students, although the association was weak and does not establish causality. The findings support consideration of structured, responsible AI literacy and innovation-focused learning activities in nursing education. Larger multi-site and longitudinal studies are needed to identify additional factors that shape innovative behaviour.

items.title: Balancing innovation and ethics: responsible governance of artificial intelligence hallucinations in healthcare
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare and may improve efficiency in clinical support, health management, and doctor-patient communication. Yet its tendency to hallucinate, that is, to generate medical information that appears plausible but is false, can create systemic ethical risks in high-risk medical settings. This paper addresses two questions: what distinctive ethical risks are created by medical AI hallucinations, and what governance mechanisms can respond to them? Using the four principles of biomedical ethics as an analytical tool, the paper identifies four risk pathways: weakened informed consent, erosion of doctor-patient trust, harm to life and health, and unfair responsibility allocation. It then introduces responsible research and innovation (RRI) to build a four-dimensional framework of anticipation, inclusion, reflexivity, and responsiveness. The main contribution of the paper is to integrate biomedical ethical principles with RRI governance tools in the specific context of medical AI hallucinations, developing a closed-loop governance matrix across technology development, clinical application, and regulatory oversight. This provides an operational pathway for moving medical AI from technical feasibility towards ethical trustworthiness.

items.title: Beyond the Question Asked: Relational Understanding, Constructive Framing, and Human Agency in Personalized AI
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is increasingly capable of generating accurate, fluent, and personalized responses. Yet a response can be factually correct and still fail the person receiving it. Human questions arise within relationships, histories, emotional states, goals, uncertainties, and boundaries. The next stage of personalized AI therefore requires more than retrieval of user preferences or stylistic imitation. It requires a disciplined capacity to interpret the likely human context beneath an explicit request while preserving truth, agency, privacy, and the user’s authority to correct the system. This paper extends Dynamic Personalized Guidance Architecture (Dynamic PGA) by proposing a relational layer, described here as Relational-Emotional Synergy (RES), and a principle of constructive framing. RES treats meaning as something that can develop across an ongoing human-AI relationship rather than within isolated prompts alone. Constructive framing adds a directional obligation: when a user is discouraged, anxious, frustrated, or uncertain, the AI should not reflexively mirror negativity or offer unearned reassurance. It should acknowledge the circumstances honestly while, where appropriate, orienting the response toward clarity, realistic possibility, agency, and a useful next step. The paper deliberately remains text-centered. Voice, prosodic emotion sensing, and deeper multimodal inference are treated as future research rather than requirements of the present framework. It also recognizes language proficiency as an accessibility boundary: depth of thought should not be confused with fluency in written English or any dominant language. The central proposition is that personalized AI should seek to understand more deeply than the literal question asked, while never claiming certainty about a person’s inner state and never allowing personalization to outrun truth or human autonomy.

items.title: Corporate Reputation Through the Lens of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The spread of assistants based on large language models (LLMs) is changing how customers, investors, candidates and other stakeholders access information about organisations. This working paper examines two distinct functions of artificial intelligence: as a diagnostic lens for identifying informational discrepancies that need to be verified, and as an intermediary that selects, summarises and sometimes recommends companies. Drawing on the literature on organisational reputation, AI-mediated communication and brand experience, and integrating the exploratory results of the Aurelian Watch 2026 Observatory (50 Italian companies; 2,450 responses), the paper proposes the concept of “Symphonic Reputation” as a strategic vision for Corporate Communication. It requires the coordination of behaviours, narratives, independent evidence, AI systems and human relationships, without confusing coherence with uniformity. The paper discusses the implications for governance, for the commercial consideration of products and services, and for events, distinguishing observations, inferences and recommendations. It expresses the perspective of Aurelian Lab; the Observatory data are descriptive and concern 50 Italian medium-sized companies.

items.title: CTI-Rationale: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Framework for Evidence-Grounded MITRE ATT&CK Technique Mapping
items.abstract: Mapping cyber-threat intelligence (CTI) to MITRE ATT&CK is usually evaluated as label prediction, yet a correct technique identifier may rest on the wrong words. We treat each mapping as an argument (a technique claim supported by textual data, a warrant, and rejected alternatives) and annotation as discovery followed by judgment. CTI-Rationale instantiates this model with 1740 expert paragraph–technique mappings from 100 public reports, each with an evidence span, free-text rationale, reasoning type, and confidence, and most with primitives and ruled-out alternatives. All rationale content was written and adjudicated by human analysts, not generated by artificial intelligence. The low paragraph-level Jaccard (0.421) is associated mainly with coverage differences, not conflicting labels: paragraphs mapped by both annotators reach 0.780, only 10.4% of one-sided mappings are conflicts, and capture–recapture estimates put gold completeness at 84.2–88.0% (likely optimistic), lowest for behavioral and contextual warrants. In cross-validation, the annotation bundle improves micro-F1 beyond an equal-volume control (+0.024 [0.013, 0.035]), also under campaign-grouped and publisher-held-out folds and in document-disjoint transfer to TRAM2; ATT&CK definition text recovers about two thirds of the gain over label-only training. Evidence-supervised span ranking improves overlap with expert evidence, which label metrics do not capture. With fully delivered prompts, retrieved demonstrations raise a smaller language model’s micro-F1 from 0.367 to 0.500 (labels) and 0.475 (full annotations; no reliable added benefit). Unlabeled chunks remain unverified candidate negatives.

items.title: Dampak Keterikatan Kerja pada Karyawan: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Work engagement is a positive mental state characterized by the dimensions of vigor, dedication, and absorption in one's work. This phenomenon is crucial in modern human resource management due to its ability to link individual psychological well-being with organizational effectiveness. This study aims to examine the impact of employees' work engagement using a systematic literature review method, where research findings were obtained from credible scientific articles sourced via Publish or Perish version 8 and selected through the Rayyan.id platform. The inclusion criteria were: articles published between 2016 and 2025, written in Indonesian, employing a quantitative design, and focusing on employees in Indonesian companies. Following the selection process, this study demonstrates that work engagement has a significant positive influence on various critical aspects of the workplace, playing a key role in reducing work-related stress by positioning well-being as the primary mediator, thereby enabling employees to achieve a state of total focus while working. These findings confirm that strengthening factors such as empowering leadership, quality of work life, and perceptions of occupational health and safety (OHS) are highly strategic in supporting the sustainability and overall competitiveness of the organization. items.title: Decision-Making Amid Information-Based Threats in Sociotechnical Systems: A Review
items.abstract: Technological systems increasingly mediate human information exchange, spanning interactions among humans as well as between humans and artificial agents. The unprecedented scale and reliance on information disseminated through these systems substantially expand the scope of information-based influence that can both enable and undermine sound decision-making. Consequently, understanding and protecting decision-making today faces growing challenges, as individuals and organizations must navigate evolving opportunities and information-based threats across varied domains and information environments. While these risks are widely recognized, research remains fragmented: work evaluating information-based threat phenomena has progressed largely in isolation from foundational studies of human information processing. In this review, we synthesize insights from both domains to identify shared cognitive mechanisms that mediate vulnerability to information-based threats and shape behavioral outcomes. Finally, we outline directions for future research aimed at integrating these perspectives, emphasizing the importance of such integration for mitigating human vulnerabilities and aligning human-machine representations.
